title: LedgerCloseMetaBatch.fromXDR refuses a valid ledger whose failed transaction carries an authorization tree at the network's maximum depth

target.versions_affected: 17.4.0 and main 81e76be (executed; js-xdr 5.0.0 DEFAULT_MAX_DEPTH 1500; range not established)

severity_basis: stellar-core 30.0.0 admits an authorization tree (subInvocations) 493 levels deep (494 is txMALFORMED), so such a failed transaction can land in a ledger. js-stellar-sdk decodes that LedgerCloseMeta (493 sits exactly at its 1500 depth budget), the TransactionEnvelope and the TransactionHistoryEntry, but LedgerCloseMetaBatch.fromXDR (the data-lake wrapper) adds levels and fails with 'max recursion depth 1500 exceeded'. No SDF service is known to be affected; the impact is on JavaScript readers of the data lake.

entries.expected: a LedgerCloseMetaBatch around a ledger the network admitted decodes
entries.observed: Not reached by this entry's ledgers (their tree is shallower). On a local stellar-core 30.0.0 ledger with an authorization tree 493 levels deep, LedgerCloseMetaBatch.fromXDR throws 'max recursion depth 1500 exceeded'; the bare LedgerCloseMeta decodes.

evidence.pre_fix: Executed by hand outside the corpus: on a local offline stellar-core 30.0.0 an authorization tree of 493 levels is accepted (494 is txMALFORMED) and recorded as a failed transaction (ledger 13); that ledger, wrapped in a LedgerCloseMetaBatch, was decoded with js-stellar-sdk 17.4.0 and main 81e76be. No corpus entry holds such a ledger yet, so no report row exists.
evidence.expected_basis: A reader of the data lake must decode every ledger the network admitted; the batch wrapper adds only a few XDR levels.

reproduction.method: Re-run on js-stellar-sdk 17.4.0 and main 81e76be with the same local stellar-core 30.0.0 ledger before filing; the batch decode fails as recorded and the bare LedgerCloseMeta decodes.

approval.scope: Public issue on stellar/js-stellar-sdk (#1901): LedgerCloseMetaBatch.fromXDR refuses a valid ledger with a 493-level authorization tree.

history.note: Created from a depth check with a local stellar-core 30.0.0. js refusing 375 or more nested ScVal vectors is not a defect: the network maximum is 246 nested vectors and host-written values stop at 99.
Filed by the maintainers of this kit as https://github.com/stellar/js-stellar-sdk/issues/1901 (17.4.0 and main 81e76be).
Upstream state refreshed: the issue is open; a fix pull request (#1902, raising the decode and encode depth limit to 1550) is open and not merged.
